features.title: Classic workspace
features.scope: Classic stage, tools, timeline, Library, Properties, Actions, Accessibility, Output (with live same-frame search filtering and filtered Copy without mutating session logs), Align, Transform, Color, Swatches, Info, Filters, Ease, History, Scene, Motion editor, Project, Compiler errors, Code snippets and Movie Explorer panels plus the modal Find and Replace dialog (⌘F) with Dark (default), Light, Mid Neutral Gray (`bg/app` `#505050`) and Dark Graphite (`bg/app` `#171717`, `timeline/grid` `#2E2E2E`) themes and density-proportional top-bar branding (`28 / 22 / 18 pt` across `48 / 40 / 32 pt` top bars). Dockable panels share a four-sided configurable dock grid with resizable areas/groups, ordered tabs, native floating windows and Window ▸ Hide panels (F4). File ▸ Open recent, Close and Revert manage recent and saved documents; Revert also reloads imported FLA/XFL/SWF sources and retains unsaved edits if reload fails, and Control ▸ Enable simple buttons (⌥⌘B) previews Button Up/Over/Down states and press/release feedback live on the authoring Stage. Stage object context actions open under every active tool, including Break apart (⌘B), Group (⌘G), Ungroup (⇧⌘G) and Trace bitmap…. Header drag supports docking, tab merging/reordering, splits and undocking, with actual panel contents previewed while the button is held over the Stage and between dock targets inside NeoFlash windows. Inactive dragged tabs preview their own contents without changing the saved active tab. Panels torn from top/bottom docks immediately reflow to their compact floating size, keeping normal text and control scale; detaching retains that preview position and size. Previously saved dock-wide sizes are bounded by the standard floating size. Saved workspace geometry is separate from document content. Actions provides frame/object/source editing and source-specific feedback. Info edits selection W/H/X/Y as one Undo step and shows live cursor coordinates in ruler units plus RGBA color under the stage pointer. Shared label/value rows and compact system fonts align controls across panels; the Library preview stays above the scrolling browser. Panels move between native windows; borderless floating windows use the shared NF2 header and retain their own tab groups and horizontal/vertical split trees. Panel-specific logical minima remain scale-correct; docked groups enforce width while floating windows also enforce height. A lone Tools window has eight persisted magnetic Stage-workspace anchors, using a narrow vertical rail at the side centres and compact horizontal layout elsewhere. Escape and source-window closure cancel an active drag. Dedicated boundary grips resize dock areas, including Timeline height; menu shortcuts use separate aligned columns. The top-level Document menu sits immediately before Window, combines Document settings with the open-document list, and Window ▸ Panels contains all panel visibility rows; Help ▸ Search functions… (F1) opens a focused fuzzy-search command palette that accepts the first keystroke and runs registered menu actions directly, while Keyboard shortcuts remains a separate editor. The illustrated Help manual keeps fixed bounds while chapters scroll and opens portable self-contained Authoring Manual and Scripting Reference browser editions on `file://` with chapter routing, structured reference tables and CSS-themed inline SVGs across all four themes. Individual tabs and complete tab groups have distinct drag handles. Floating Edit/Dock commands live in the compact header menu. Numeric controls support click/type and drag/scrub. Properties chooses object, Timeline, Stage or active-tool context automatically, without a Selection/Tool switch; semantically paired value rows across Properties, Transform/Color, Text, Filters, Motion, Info, Accessibility, tool panels and Sound Properties share equal responsive cells with the NF2 S2 gap and an 80 pt minimum, keep trailing controls inside their own cell, keep colour swatch+hex beside alpha, and stack left before right below the fit threshold; a blank Stage click clears Timeline frame/range focus so the Background control is directly available; Library keeps search and commands fixed around one scrolling list. Native palettes are bundled from the shared design tokens. All panels use the common control density and semantic themes, bounded menus with aligned shortcuts, and explicit overflow controls. Fresh compact workspaces group Library and Properties without replacing saved custom layouts. Older saved live built-in layouts refresh once when the canonical NF2 composition changes, while theme, editor preferences and named layout presets are preserved. View ▸ Rulers / Grid / Guides, zoom-control toggles and the Rulers, guides & grid popover share one setting state; Save as default stores it in the editor preferences. The Stage breadcrumb opens the Symbols & scenes popover (with live search, Scenes, Matches, Recent, expandable folders, keyboard ↑↓ / ←→ / ↵ / ⌥↵ navigation and … overflow). The Stage shows NF2 tool and handle cursors and NF2 selection/transform boxes, anchors and marquee in all four themes. Preferences (⌘U) and Keyboard shortcuts (⌥⇧⌘K) persist General (four-theme live preview with Save/Cancel restoration, UI scale, on launch + File ▸ Open recent, undo levels, autosave/recovery, tooltip shortcuts, Shift-select), Code editor, Timeline, Drawing, Text, Clipboard, Shortcuts (106-command registry, custom sets, key recording, conflict detection, HTML export) and Publish settings. Grid settings offer Dynamic (default: page-aware colour/opacity and adaptive display density) and Static (fixed manual colour/spacing), retaining the configured snapping step and saved manual colour. New/Open insert tabs after the active document; opening an already open native or imported source activates its tab without reloading. Document tabs, the Window list and keyboard cycling retain independent selection, playhead, drafts, Undo and recovery. Close others, Close all and Quit ask for dirty documents in tab order; Cancel or failed Save stops on the prompted tab and preserves deferred discard decisions. Closing the last tab shows New document/Open and disables document commands. Named workspace Save/Replace/Update/Rename/Delete/Reset stores complete dock and floating-window layouts independently of documents and global tool preferences. The window notification host stacks at most three notices above the canvas or status bar, delays them during modals, coalesces repeats, pauses expiry on hover and retains messages in Output; drawing refusals and Save/internal Reload errors are connected. Customize tools edits global tool groups with draft Add/Remove/reorder, Restore default and OK/Cancel.
features.limitations: Main-window side groups remain stacked rows/columns; arbitrary recursive main-window splits remain unavailable. Output history belongs to each session and is not a persistent disk log; broader operation-specific notification routing is not complete. VoiceOver/IME and mixed-DPI monitors need broader platform acceptance. Follow-system theme, custom syntax colour schemes and controls awaiting NF2 design decisions or standalone subsystems stay disabled. Dynamic grid contrast follows the page background rather than each artwork pixel. Static preserves manual colour/opacity and hides only an axis whose fixed spacing is below one screen point. Commands/.nfsl execution remains undefined. Brush/Pencil headers use the existing shared TypeHeader until its approved compact variant is supplied; unsupported brush and stroke options remain disabled.

features.title: Library and nested editing
features.scope: Reusable instances and nested editing preserve authored identity and scripts. Edit in place resolves one exact visible placement, composes its invertible affine transform through nested levels, dims the frozen parent context and inverse-maps rendering, picking, selection, transforms, vector tools, drops, snapping and motion overlays; clean isolated definition editing remains a separate route. The session restores each level's playhead, active layer, selection, zoom/pan, ruler zero, frame range and Timeline focus, including paused independent-clip frames. A double-click on genuinely empty canvas with no active draft/gesture consumes the full press/release gesture and leaves exactly one hierarchy level without changing the sticky tool or immediately reopening the restored child; repeating the gesture continues upward. Entering a MovieClip by double-click requires an actual hit on that placement. Breadcrumbs retain direct navigation. Convert to Symbol offers aligned name/type/folder, nine-point registration and export identifier/existing-class fields. The Library shows a real first-frame preview, persistent folders, inline and drag-and-drop folder/symbol organization (`drag_drop_symbol_to_folder`, `drag_drop_folder_to_folder`), search by name/path/linkage/class, Name/Type/Linkage sorting and visible linkage, plus Select unused items, Delete unused items, bulk folder moves and bulk symbol-type changes in one Undo step. Duplicate symbol clones non-scene symbols with fresh IDs and cleared linkage (including Stage context-menu `Duplicate symbol…` and Properties `Duplicate…` on a selected instance); Delete symbol removes the symbol and cleans up any placed instances across timelines in one Undo step; Swap symbol in the Library, Stage context-menu `Swap symbol…`, Properties `Swap…` symbol-picker popover or holding ⌥ (Alt) while dragging a symbol from the Library onto the Stage or a Timeline layer row/frame span replaces the symbol on the selected stage instance or active/hovered layer across its keyframes while preserving transform, name, scripts, filters, blend mode and compatible playback. Selected symbol-instance Properties also exposes behavior switching (`Movie Clip` / `Button` / `Graphic`), `Edit symbol`, `Position and size` (`X`/`Y`, `W`/`H` + `Constrain instance proportions`, `Scale X`/`Scale Y`, `Rotation`/`Skew`), `Colour effect` (`Style: None / Brightness / Tint / Advanced / Alpha`), `Display` and `Filters`, and `Break Apart` (`⌘B` or Stage context menu) expands a MovieClip, Button or Graphic instance into the evaluated child elements, groups and bitmap fills of its visible layers at the current frame. Symbols also support 9-slice scaling grids (`Scale9Mapping`, keeping the 4 corner regions unstretched while scaling edge and centre regions inversely to the instance's `scale_x`/`scale_y`, with interactive Stage 9-slice guide dragging, live clamping, `Escape` cancellation and 1-Undo) and portable Shared Library linkage (`SharedLibraryLinkage` in `library/shared_libraries.json`, `set_symbol_shared_library`, `sync_shared_library`, and external `.nflash` donor selection via the file chooser). Folder paths survive symbol clipboard transfers; conflicts reject before mutation. Empty symbol creation opens nested editing. Buttons expose Up/Over/Down/Hit, instance actions and authored/export-linked SimpleButton typing. Library Properties changes kind across references while preserving keys/scripts and refusing incompatible class linkage.
features.limitations: Edit in place refuses singular/non-finite transforms and non-affine 9-slice scaling instead of mutating geometry in the wrong coordinate space. Local guides and grid work for axis-preserving and quarter-turn mappings. The ruler uses local values only when both mapped axes increase screen-right/down and otherwise falls back to screen values; signed/reflected labels, arbitrary oblique/skewed chrome and the corresponding affine Brush cursor await the locked NF2 contract in R-063. Dedicated ⌥-drag replacement badges wait for NF2 request R-041. Arbitrary runtime state-object assignment and empty SimpleButton construction remain unsupported. Multi-object conversion requires a contiguous stack on one layer. Preview is the first frame. Resource files remain outside the symbol-folder tree.

features.title: Authored text
features.scope: The Stage Text tool creates point text on click and a fixed, multiline wrapping TextBox on drag. Editable authored TextBox supports logical dimensions, installed regular/bold/italic fonts, size/color/leading, left/center/right/justify alignment, per-range rich-text `TextFormatRun` persistence, HTML/CSS authoring (`set_selected_text_html` / `selected_text_to_html`), authored dynamic/input field options (`AuthoredTextFieldOptions`: `field_type`, `selectable`, `editable`, `border`, `background`, `password`, `max_chars`, `restrict`, `html`, `condense_white`, `auto_size`), `set_selected_text_auto_size` (`"none"`, `"left"`, `"center"`, `"right"` resizing and anchoring in one Undo step) and conversion through characters to editable installed-font glyph contours. Selected TextBox Properties uses a compact classic Flash two-column inspector: `Text type` (`Static Text` / `Dynamic Text` / `Input Text`) and `Family` on one row; `Style` (`Regular` / `Bold` / `Italic` / `Bold Italic`), `Embed font` and `Embedding…` on one row (opening the existing NF2 dialog on the exact selected Family/Style, saving ranges/custom characters and committing the font resource plus field setting as one Undo step); `Size` (`pt`) and `Letter spacing` (`px`) on one row; `Color` and `Auto kern` on one row; compact `Selectable` / `HTML` / `Border` / `Underline` switches; `Paragraph` with 4-mode `Segmented` alignment, two-column `Indent` + `Line` spacing, two-column `Left` + `Right` margins and `Behavior` (`Single line` / `Multiline` / `Multiline no wrap` / `Password`); and collapsible `Options` (`URL`, two-column `Target` + `Max chars`, two-column `Variable` + `Restrict`). Old unboxed Text retains its appearance until explicit conversion. AS3 TextField/TextFormat and AS2 createTextField share Rust state and line layout, with separate current/insertion formats and bounded whole-field/string editing. Scripted HTML5 input adds native browser editing, Rust revision-checked user transactions, UTF-16 selection/replacement, user-only restrict/maxChars and password masking. AS3 TextFieldType/TextEvent/FocusEvent and AS2 Selection/onChanged/focus callbacks share Stage focus and publication lifetime. Native inline Stage editing adds UTF-16 caret/range selection, keyboard and text insertion, clipboard operations, exact mixed-run character formatting, paragraph-range expansion, collapsed-caret typing format and one Undo per accepted edit.
features.limitations: Advanced paragraphs and full shaping/Flash metrics remain incomplete. Ligature execution uses a bounded substitution profile and browser font-feature requests rather than a complete OpenType shaping engine. Locale casing has explicit Turkic/Greek rules plus a same-UTF-16-length Unicode fallback; length-changing mappings are retained unchanged, and the native locale selector exposes only its fixed language list. Host font measurements may produce different line breaks and pixels; portable fonts are separate work. Native headless layout/clipping/Undo and in-app-browser reflow/alignment, independent fields and Restart passed. Native inline selection/editing and mixed-run formatting are implemented; VERIFICATION.md preserves the exact scope separately from earlier plain-text evidence. Independent fba17ae evidence (TEXT-LAYOUT-HTML5-20261027T0409Z) covers only the actual uniform layout/format/refusal/Restart workflow in VERIFICATION.md. That earlier browser pass does not by itself establish other fonts/engines or native input/IME. The separate text-form delivery records current scripted input evidence; earlier layout evidence is unchanged. The active DOM field follows affine/vector clipping but is above foreground Canvas artwork. Full IME/locale/grapheme/original-player behavior and cross-engine metrics remain pending; AS2 general string target resolution is unsupported.

features.title: Advanced vector tools
features.scope: Line, PolyStar (polygon/star with modal sides and star point-size settings), vector Brush with eight tip shapes, document-unit size (1–200 px), zoom-aware cursor, smoothing, pressure size control, tilt angle toggle, all 5 Flash Brush paint modes (`Paint normal`, `Paint fills`, `Paint behind`, `Paint selection`, `Paint inside`), Lock fill and Option+Command-drag resize; Round/Flat/Chisel and custom user brush presets (`New brush` / `Delete brush`); Brush retains stroke RGB/alpha/gradient at zero width and Merge Drawing preserves dormant stroke paint during normalization; independent Pencil Straighten/Smooth/Ink modes and smoothing strength (drawing tools stay selected across consecutive gestures). Paint Bucket fills a bounded planar face formed by one or several contours and applies its per-contour gap choice (0/6/14/28 screen pixels); Ink Bottle can add the active solid/gradient stroke to an otherwise transparent contour; solid-color Eyedropper stays active after sampling. Eraser defaults to cutting through raw Merge fills and Bézier strokes with swept geometry, while whole-object/fill/stroke modes remain explicit choices; its cursor is the complete gesture preview and touched objects are never outlined with target boxes. Lasso defaults to splitting and selecting partial raw Merge fills/strokes, and a rectangular marquee applies the same split so Backspace removes only the selected segment; Object Drawing placements and groups remain whole. Each successful gesture is one Undo step. Pen closes on its first anchor; Escape finishes a valid open path without switching tools so the next click starts another path. Hand/temporary Space pan, zoom and fill gradient transform remain available. Object Drawing and planar Merge Drawing modes (`J`, Tool options, Preferences ▸ Drawing ▸ Default mode): Merge Drawing separates fill and stroke into independent elements (`Element.merge` in format 7), subtracts overlapping different-color fills, unions overlapping same-color fills without a separating stroke, slices fills crossed by strokes, splits intersecting strokes at intersection points, re-merges moved Merge shapes on drop with bounded same-paint batches, local overlap indexes and atomic rollback on geometry failure, selects adjacent/connected strokes on double-click, and clips the existing shape-selection hatch to visible fill/stroke geometry and authored masks. Pen click on a selected path segment subdivides to insert an anchor, and Subselection Delete/Backspace or ⌥-click deletes selected anchors while preserving curve continuity. Internal triangulation edges do not split artwork; coincident outlines remain connected and transformed gradients retain their appearance. Authoring groups preserve runtime identities and isolate their Merge members from raw drawing; Modify and the Stage context menu provide arrange, Combine objects (Union, Intersect, Punch, Crop), classic Group (`⌘G`, grouping 1+ selected objects on the same layer or across multiple layers onto the topmost selected layer in back-to-front visual order, materializing a keyframe on held frames and assigning fresh IDs when an element still exists on other keyframes of its source layer), Ungroup (`⇧⌘G`), Break Apart (`⌘B`, breaking apart authoring groups, MovieClip/Button/Graphic instances at their evaluated child frame, Bitmap placements into bitmap-filled Merge paths, parametric primitives, Object Drawing paths and Text / TextBox elements), transforms and group-aware alignment/distribution with exact gaps. Stage rulers, per-timeline ruler guides and a stage grid; moves, transform handles, rectangles, ovals, lines, pen anchors and path points snap to guides, objects, grid and pixels with a snap ring, configurable accuracy and ⌘-suspend. Moving selections preserve Guides > Objects > Grid > Pixels priority across all edges/centres, then choose the nearest target within that family on each axis. Grid visibility and snapping are independent. Trace bitmap converts one selected bitmap to editable coloured vector paths with cancellable live preview, colour/palette presets, Paths/Corners/Noise, Abutting/Overlapping, fills/strokes, Snap curves and Ignore white. Full tracing preserves placement and the tool, groups multicolour results and commits one Undo; a single-colour compound path retains holes and islands. Free Transform Envelope (4×4 Coons patch handles) and Perspective (2×2 corner handles), Asset Warp (W) Stage pin creation/dragging/deletion with mesh overlay, and IK Bone/Bind Stage bone creation, CCD effector dragging and contour vertex binding commit as single Undo steps.
features.limitations: Tablet pressure and tilt depend on native macOS tablet-point events from the device driver. Brush/Pencil compact TypeHeader needs a shared NF2 API. Bucket fills bounded vector faces but does not perform bitmap flood fill. Default cut-through of both fills and strokes is limited to raw Merge geometry; Object Drawing retains conservative stroke-segment behavior. Partial cuts approximate touched curves and refuse masked targets, combined fill/stroke effects and unsafe guided auto-key insertion; refusal cancels the whole gesture and gives a Warning notification plus Output. Group requires current-keyframe members. The View snapping submenu and nested group editing remain separate. Trace is approximate vectorization, bounded to 4096×4096, 20,000 colours/contours, 1,000,000 boundary edges and 100,000 commands per colour. Full palette retains exact source RGBA; Automatic uses at most 30 colours. Translucent source/placement uses disjoint boundaries to avoid added alpha. Bitmap scripts, filters, non-Normal blending, cache effects and unsafe guided auto-key insertion are refused explicitly. Deco, Spray Brush, Bone, Bind, Asset Warp (W) and 3D Translation (G) / Rotation are reachable from F1 Function Search, shortcuts, Customize tools and contextual Properties; IK Bone and Bind use bounded CCD solving and contour-vertex weight assignment rather than multi-branch physics simulation.

features.title: Binary FLA to editable document
features.scope: Native conversion for Flash 3, 5, MX, 8, CS3 and CS4 preserves scenes, library folders and symbols, ordered layers with masks, folders and motion guides, held keys, nested instances with graphic first-frame offsets, display filters (`DropShadow`, `Blur`, `Glow`, `Bevel`, `GradientGlow`, `GradientBevel` and `AdjustColor` / `ColorMatrix`), blend modes, `cacheAsBitmap` and visibility (`Element.{filters, blend_mode, cache_as_bitmap, visible}` in format 7), 3D placement perspective projection into 2D affine transforms, classic, shape and CS4 motion-object / IK pose-keyframe tweens with easing, text, PNG/JPEG bitmaps, uncompressed PCM and compressed Flash ADPCM (`codec_id == 1`, 2/3/4/5-bit mono and stereo decoded to 16-bit PCM `audio/wav`) and MP3 (`audio/mpeg`) sound resources, `CPicFrame` timeline frame sounds (`Event`/`Start`/`Stop`/`Stream` sync, repeats/loop-forever, preset effects, format-7 custom multi-point stereo envelopes via `SoundEffect::Custom` / `FrameSound.envelope` and `in_point`/`out_point` trim windows), `CMediaVideoData` / `CPicVideo` video resources and `TimelineVideoSpan` placements, and ActionScript (legacy Actions-panel commands translated to AS1). Features the model cannot express yet are approximated or kept as visible placeholders, each with a located warning; the original FLA is embedded in parts when it fits, and oversized documents fit within the 128 MiB project JSON budget by shedding largest media first, compacting provenance placement tables and degrading excess later vector paths to placeholders with warnings. The recorded private corpus survey imports 105 of 106 documents; successful conversions have save/reopen coverage, without establishing visual or behavioral parity with Flash.
features.limitations: Convolution filters, rare legacy audio codecs (GSM/Nellymoser/Speex), raw FLV/Sorenson video streams without embedded container headers, dynamic/input and nonuniform rich text runs, and component behavior are approximated with warnings. Documents whose converted media and geometry exceed the 128 MiB project JSON limit shed oversized media or later vector paths to placeholders rather than streaming unbounded assets. Font metrics may differ; output is not claimed pixel-identical to Flash. Supported 3D placements are projected into 2D with a located warning; this is an approximation, not preserved 3D behavior.

features.title: SWF inspection
features.scope: Recognizes FWS/CWS/ZWS signatures, validates container bounds, decompresses `CWS` zlib and `ZWS` LZMA1 (SWF 13+) streams up to 64 MiB, parses stage `RECT` bounds, 8.8 fixed-point frame rate and frame count, decodes dictionary/display/media/font/button/scene tags into a validated NeoFlash `Project` (and `.fla` XFL 2.2 archive via `export_fla`), and statically decompiles AVM1 (`DoAction`, `DoInitAction`, button and clip actions → AS1/AS2) and AVM2 (`DoABC`/`DoABC2` → AS3 `.as` classes and `addFrameScript` timeline frame scripts) without executing bytecode (`ImportReport.swf`). A separate SwfBytecodePlayer executes a bounded AVM1/AVM2 subset; static import itself does not execute bytecode.
features.limitations: Direct AVM1/AVM2 bytecode execution is intentionally not performed by the importer; filters, blend modes, non-quad bitmap fills, dynamic/non-vector `clip_depth` masks, Nellymoser/Speex audio and video streams are approximated or represented as reported placeholders. The bytecode player does not implement the complete AVM1/AVM2 instruction or coercion contracts: unknown AVM1 operations can be skipped, and AVM2 loose and strict equality share one implementation.

features.title: Independent project format
features.scope: Versioned JSON stores stable symbols/placements/frames/scripts; version 2 adds logical project source units and document/symbol linkage with path, size and reference validation. Existing version-1 projects remain supported. Version 3 adds portable resource bytes, normalized logical paths/types, strict base64/size validation and shared immutable storage across native snapshots; versions 1 and 2 remain readable. Authored Bitmap elements reference portable PNG/JPEG resource IDs with validated intrinsic dimensions; mutable runtime pixels stay outside the document. TextBox stores explicit layout dimensions and uniform formatting; legacy Text remains readable without conversion, and runtime insertion defaults stay outside authored state. Format 4 adds authored layer roles/relationships and logical library folders with backward-compatible defaults. Format 5 adds affine skew, inherited color transforms, authored gradient paths, Flash easing and an explicit AS1 script identity. Format 6 adds multi-scene lists, tween kinds, motion property keys, motion and ruler guides and frame sounds. Format 7 adds parametric rectangle corner radii, oval start/end angles, inner radius and close-path options (`Transform.primitive`), custom transform pivots (`Transform.pivot`), Bounce and Elastic ease presets (`Easing::{Bounce, Elastic}`), per-property motion eases (`Keyframe.property_eases`), motion graphic synchronization and guide snapping (`Keyframe.{sync_symbols, snap_to_guide}`), custom stereo sound envelopes and playback trim windows (`SoundEffect::Custom`, `FrameSound.{envelope, in_point, out_point}`), and authored display filters, blend modes, `cacheAsBitmap` and visibility (`Element.{filters, blend_mode, cache_as_bitmap, visible}`). Format 8 adds editable spatial Motion paths, classic endpoint snapping, layer blending and synchronized layer timelines. Format 9 adds painted mask modes/inversion, per-resource export settings, roving Motion keys and live Stage authoring controls for Envelope (4×4), Perspective (2×2), Asset Warp and IK armatures. Format 10 adds sparse stable-ID `motion_tracks` and authoritative per-object `motion_keys`, while documents without them retain their exact legacy shared settings and paths. Format 11 adds layer/keyframe display-filter stacks and External/Progressive timeline-video deployment. Format 12 adds authored timeline-video out-points. Document ▸ Document settings… (⌘J) edits stage size, Match contents, anchored content scaling, units, background and frame rate in one Undo step and saves new-document defaults in workspace prefs; a blank Stage click clears Timeline frame/range focus so Properties exposes the Stage Background control.
features.limitations: Additional media consumers, embedded font layout and broader asset dependency authoring remain separate work. Independent c39a29e acceptance (RESOURCES-HTML5-20261027T0323Z) covers the precise embedded/HTTP and pending-request observations in VERIFICATION.md; native resource authoring and full network semantics remain unverified. Independent 1bd0e3c evidence (BITMAP-HTML5-20261027T0345Z) is restricted to the PNG/shared pixel, AS2 attachment, disposal and Restart observations in VERIFICATION.md. JPEG, rasterization options, alpha hits and native image authoring do not inherit that pass.

features.title: Save and open projects
features.scope: The editor saves and opens .nflash through serialization and validation without tying the document to absolute paths, opens .swf/.fla/.xfl directly into an editable project, exports versioned .fla/XFL through target-profile preflight, and exports a bounded standalone .swf movie with structural re-import verification. Save As .fla creates a modern Animate compatibility copy without retargeting the open native document, replacing its saved snapshot, clearing dirty/recovery state or changing its recent-project identity. Native, FLA/XFL and SWF writers preflight supported fidelity, reserve a unique adjacent temporary file and atomically replace the destination only after a validated result is complete.
features.limitations: FLA/XFL and SWF are compatibility exports rather than lossless Flash/Animate round trips. The other versioned FLA and uncompressed XFL profiles are explicit File ▸ Export routes. FLA/XFL reports its 120 fps ceiling. SWF accepts a bounded script subset, proven PNG and PCM-WAV/MP3 media layouts, and supported static text outlines; unsupported field semantics, codecs, record capacities and frame rates block before writing. Unsupported filters, video or script syntax block or produce a located approximation according to the selected profile; they are never silently discarded. Autosave, recovery and multiple documents are tracked separately.

features.title: Work protection and recovery
features.scope: Close, Close all and macOS Quit activate dirty documents in tab order for Save/Discard/Cancel; earlier discard decisions take effect only after the whole sequence is approved. Cancel and failed Save leave the prompted document active with all earlier work and recovery intact. New/Open/Import create accessible tabs and preserve existing work; opening the same native/imported source activates its current tab. When On launch is set to Previous session, NeoFlash validates and restores the saved multi-tab document set and active tab on relaunch without duplicating recovered documents or suppressing crash-recovery prompts. Periodic autosave writes dirty documents atomically to `<app_support>/Recovery` every configured N minutes, cleans recovery on save/discard/normal quit and offers Restore/Discard at launch. Each restored copy opens independently; a path conflict creates an unnamed durable copy, and unanswered candidates survive Quit. Failed loading and cancelled pickers preserve existing documents; failed save formatting rolls back and successful formatting is one Undo step. Throttled file fingerprints surface per-tab Modified, Replaced or Deleted conflicts for active and inactive documents. Reload validates before replacing memory, Keep editing preserves the document, Save As preserves both versions, and ordinary Save is guarded against overwriting a conflicting disk state.
features.limitations: The external-change workflow is polling-based rather than an operating-system change stream; conflict actions remain explicit so outside changes are never silently discarded.
